A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASTGI forecasting framework, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The experimental setup in v1 Appendix A matches v2 Appendix B; v2 adds further appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting comparisons on four datasets, component ablations, and parameter sensitivity results in Tables 1–2 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds analyses of learned interaction graphs and embeddings using MIMIC test samples in Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.6 retain the same encoders, causal nearest-neighbor construction, relation-aware propagation, query prediction, and MSE objective. The new visualizations analyze existing components rather than introduce procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC, PhysioNet, Human Activity, and USHCN for forecasting, with unchanged dataset descriptions. The new qualitative analyses reuse MIMIC test data without introducing another task, population, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the identical twelve-baseline comparison, including GraFITi and Hi-Patch. Baseline adaptations match between v1 Appendix A.2 and v2 Appendix B.2; the new appendices introduce no additional comparator.

E3.justification: Appendices C–D introduce protocols for inspecting a randomly selected MIMIC test sample's graph and projecting sample coordinates into two dimensions using t-SNE. Existing forecasting splits, metrics, training budgets, and early stopping settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds two limited qualitative investigations: learned synchronous and lagged graph connections, and variable/time structure in learned embeddings (Figures 5–6). These sample-based analyses supplement the unchanged component ablations and hyperparameter sensitivity studies.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent seeds, 2024–2028, and report means and standard deviations. The new qualitative analyses add no repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 4 retain identical numerical results and sensitivity curves. Figures 5–6 add qualitative findings, including a reported Troponin I connection from t=4 to t=7 and variable/time patterns in embeddings; no quantitative forecasting improvement is newly reported.

T1.justification: The forecasting definitions and Equations 1–9 are unchanged. Appendix D restates the existing coordinate construction for visualization; neither version provides additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, four contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about avoiding representation distortion, learning adaptive interactions, and outperforming forecasting baselines. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly links representation distortion to impaired dependency modeling in the introduction. Appendices C–D add interpretations connecting attention patterns to physiological relationships and embedding structure to preserved timing and meaningful neighborhoods; these specific arguments are absent from v1.

D1.justification: The new appendices document visualization procedures, including strongest-edge filtering, attention-based node sizing, coordinate extraction, and t-SNE projection. Existing hardware, optimization, and baseline configuration disclosures are retained, with no new code or data access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 substantially narrows the cited background by removing broad regular-forecasting, NLP, vision, and diffusion references, alongside Liu et al. (2025c) on irregular forecasting. It adds application references by Yao et al. (2018) and Vio et al. (2013), while retaining the central IMTS taxonomy and technical comparisons.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work openings are rewritten, affiliations are expanded, and ethics and LLM-use statements are added. New explanatory appendices extend the narrative, but the method, experimental discussion, contribution statements, and conclusion remain largely verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document template with narrower content, resized figures and tables, running headers, and revised title and heading typography. It adds Figures 5–6, including text wrapping around the embedding plot. Existing figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The more focused introductory framing and new MIMIC graph and embedding examples modestly improve clarity and make the framework easier to inspect. Their evidential benefit is limited: some interpretations concerning physiological influence and preservation of temporal intervals exceed what single-sample visualizations establish. The central method and quantitative validation remain unchanged.
